title: Ames: a real working of God joined to moral suasion
source_text: LV. Hanc sententiam tradit & explicat Amesius in Bellarmino enervato libro tertio de Gratia capite tertio. Nos dicimus, inquit, una cum suasione morali conjungi etiam realem efficientiam Dei, qua novum principium spiritualis vitae cordi hominis efficaciter vocati ingeneratur, & homo simul excitatur ad hujus vitae actus eliciendos.
pass_a_gloss: LV. This opinion Amesius hands down & explains in Bellarminus enervatus book three on Grace chapter three. We say, he says, that together with moral suasion there is joined also a real efficiency of God, by which a new principle of spiritual life is begotten in the heart of a man efficaciously called, & the man at the same time is stirred up to elicit the acts of this life.
pass_b_english: Thesis LV. Amesius sets out and explains this view in Bellarminus enervatus, book 3, on grace, chapter 3. 'We say,' he writes, 'that along with moral persuasion there is also a real causal working of God.
By it a new source of spiritual life is planted in the heart of the person who is effectively called, and at the same time he is roused to perform the acts of this life.'
